ask: Build the machine-load brake as a standing part of claude-settings, on every device that installs it (Windows and Mac, no admin): at the moment a lane is about to start, the guard reads the machine's load once and sets how many lanes may run.
note: Done. Rulings: every device that installs claude-settings; no watcher, timer, per-call reading or log of its own (Oct 21); no lane or process count (Oct 22); disk busy under the smaller of 10% and 15 GB free, full under the smaller of 5% and 5 GB (Oct 23); CPU dropped, since a short sample is noise (Oct 25). Landed: #562, #565, #569, then #572 (the brake reads memory and disk only; decision machine-load-brake rewritten). Related: c40 (idle desktop sessions each burn a core).
title: Machine-load brake: every session paces its lanes to the device's real load
why: Your idea, Oct 20, widened Oct 21: when the machine is loaded, sessions slow down; when it has room, more lanes can run. Incidents: the 15 spinning claude.exe workers of Oct 19, the q_max load report, and the Windows RAM climb to about 98% of Oct 21. Your caution, Oct 21: measuring and logging have cost more than the problem before.
